question.text: Dividend income received by a resident individual is taxed at:

answer.text: The applicable income-tax slab rate, with TDS at 10% on resident dividend if the amount exceeds INR 10,000

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the workbook, dividend income is taxable in the hands of the shareholders at the applicable tax rate. For a resident classified under "Others", dividends are taxed at the slab rate, and resident dividend attracts TDS at 10% where the amount exceeds INR 10,000. The Trap: A flat 10% rate or a flat 20% rate ignores the slab-based treatment in shareholders' hands. "Zero" reflects the pre-reform DDT-era thinking, which is no longer the position in the workbook. Note: Two figures to keep separate: the income is taxed at slab rates, while the TDS rate is 10% with a threshold of INR 10,000 for resident dividend.
